entries.capability: Transactional emails state what was bought and what it cost

evidence.observation: all four transactional emails for the seeded order (confirmation, invoice, shipment, credit memo) render and name the order, its addresses, payment and shipping method, and carry no item table, no line, no subtotal and no amount at all: a customer is told their order was placed without being told what they bought or what they paid. Captured in mailcatcher on 2026-08-26 from order 000000076, 3.8-4.0 KB each. Rendering the sales_email_order_items handle through the layout directly produces no blocks either, which points at the same cause; reproduce with npm run emails:send && npm run emails:verify

entries.reason: real gap: the sales_email_* handles MageObsidian re-declares contribute no content to the rendered email

entries.capability: The category page does not pay a url_rewrite lookup per category in the menu

evidence.observation: the reported shape — 153 of 207 queries on a category page being one url_rewrite N+1 in the menu — does not reproduce. Instrumented with tools/perf/measure-queries.ts against a cold block_html cache and 289 categories in the menu: 183 queries on the listing, 15 of them on url_rewrite (8%), and only 4 attributed to the menu. MenuTree::load seeds every category's request_path through RequestPathResolver::seed, which is a single UrlFinder::findAllByData for the whole tree; the 4 are one per nav rendering (primary, mobile, footer, and the depth-limited variant), not one per category

entries.resolvedBy: module-storefront commits 13161a4 'perf(storefront): batch category url rewrite lookups into one query' and 0f0859f 'perf(storefront): cache the menu tree in block_html with a 1h ttl', both 2026-07-27; re-measured 2026-08-26 with pnpm perf:queries and asserted by perf-queries.perf.spec.ts
tests: perf-queries.perf.spec.ts:plp renders inside its query ceiling

entries.capability: The checkout page is served from the edge cache and still carries nothing private

evidence.observation: unlike checkout_cart_index, the migrated checkout_index_index declares no cacheable="false", and Varnish answers /checkout/ with x-magento-cache-debug: HIT. It is deliberate, not an omission: CheckoutConfig::getInlineConfig writes only the public half into the page while the page is cacheable, and the quote arrives through the obsidian-checkout section that SectionPrefetchRuntime prefetches. Held to that by a test that fails if the shell ever stops being cacheable or starts carrying the customer's data

entries.capability: A search term that has never been asked for is rendered without the page cache

evidence.observation: the first request for any search term answers x-magento-cache-debug: UNCACHEABLE and only later requests for the same term become cacheable; measured 2026-08-26 on /catalogsearch/result/?q=<fresh term>. It is core Magento behaviour, not something the migrated storefront introduces, and it is why the cold protocol accepts UNCACHEABLE as well as MISS for that page

entries.capability: Every value the theme emits unescaped is classified with the origin of the value and why it is safe

evidence.observation: 207 unescaped output points across 151 templates (185 distinct once the same expression in the same file and context is counted once), extracted on 2026-08-26. The sweep covers both engines: the .twig templates the migration wrote and the 25 .phtml templates the theme still keeps — four of its own and twenty-one inherited from theme-base that this theme does not override. A first pass that read only .twig reported 162 across 147 and missed 45 points in 4 files; the structural comparison against the reference is what turned that up. 167 are covered by eleven declared rules and 18 are classified by hand against the code that produces the value. The plain text search finds 164 |raw in .twig because two of them sit inside Twig comments and never reach the output. By emission context: 191 text, 7 attribute, 5 tag, 2 script, 2 style. The PHP templates escape at assignment rather than at the echo, which is why they carry @noEscape; each one was followed back to its assignment.

tests: unescaped-output.guest.spec.ts:no unescaped output point is unclassified, and none carries end-user content without a guarantee

entries.capability: A product attribute value reaches the page through the same output filter core uses

evidence.observation: two templates print a product attribute value unescaped and skip Magento\Catalog\Helper\Output::productAttribute, which core applies at the same positions: Magento_Catalog/templates/product/view.twig:147 (the spec list, against core's attributes.phtml:27) and Magento_Catalog/templates/product/compare/list.twig:39 (against core's compare/list.phtml:132). The helper escapes every attribute that is not on the allowed-HTML list and resolves CMS directives, so the theme is less strict than the platform it replaced. The value is administrator content rather than shopper content, which is why this is major and not critical; the same divergence also means {{media url=...}} inside an attribute never resolves.

entries.reason: found by reading both sides; not yet exercised end to end because this store has no free-text attribute marked visible on the front, so a live proof would need the fixture to create one
tests: unescaped-output.guest.spec.ts:the defects the audit already found are still exactly the ones recorded

entries.capability: A search term comes back to the shopper the way they typed it

evidence.observation: MageObsidian\Storefront\ViewModel\SearchForm::getQueryValue returns Magento\Search\Helper\Data::getEscapedQueryText, which is already HTML-escaped. Twig escapes it a second time everywhere it is used outside the one |raw site, so searching for "Ben & Jerry" shows "Ben & Jerry" in the header search box, in the breadcrumb and in the SearchAutocomplete island's props. Reproduced 2026-08-26 on /catalogsearch/result/?q=Ben+%26+Jerry. It is a correctness defect, not an injection: the value is over-escaped, never under-escaped.

entries.reason: the fix is to return the unescaped query text and let the template escape it once, which is a change to MageObsidian and needs approval before it is made
tests: embedded-data.guest.spec.ts:a search term with an ampersand comes back the way the shopper typed it

entries.capability: The calls the islands make authorise as the customer they claim to be

evidence.observation: customers/me, carts/mine/totals and carts/mine/payment-methods all answer 401 without a session and 200 with one; another customer's account answers 401 to a signed-in customer and returns no data; a guest cart addressed with a mask nobody minted, with a numeric quote id, or with an empty mask is refused. Session authorisation depends on X-Requested-With: XMLHttpRequest, which Magento\Webapi\Model\Plugin\Authorization\CustomerSessionUserContext requires and a cross-origin form cannot set — so the same header that makes the islands work also keeps a cross-site request out.

tests: island-authorization.guest.spec.ts:the customer's own account is refused without a session
island-authorization.spec.ts:another customer's account is refused to a signed-in customer
island-authorization.spec.ts:a signed-in customer cannot reach their own cart through the guest door

entries.capability: The storefront runs under an enforcing content security policy

evidence.observation: under an enforcing policy of self and nothing else, every public page violates three directives. seventeen distinct fragments, all emitted by the theme or by core, none by a third party: eight inline scripts (the import map, the speculation rules, and the PREPAINT, I18N, SECTIONS, SECTION_PREFETCH, UX and ICONS runtime seeds), four inline stylesheets (the v-cloak rule, the view-transition rules, NavOverflow::getStyle, and core's per-image sizing rule) and five families of inline style attributes (display, the fluid type scale, swatch colours, view-transition names and computed widths). What none of them carry is a nonce. The storefront does keep working with all of them blocked — a shopper can still add to the cart with no page error — so this is what stands between the deployment and an enforcing policy, not a broken page.

entries.reason: closing it means threading Magento's CSP nonce through the runtime seeds and moving the per-element style attributes onto classes or custom properties, which is a change to MageObsidian and needs approval before it is made
tests: csp.guest.spec.ts:home violates nothing that is not declared
csp.guest.spec.ts:a shopper can still buy under the policy, even with every inline fragment blocked

entries.capability: The environment a security check ran in is declared, and a relaxed control makes the check non-conclusive

evidence.observation: tools/security/environment.php reports the mode, the store and every control this deployment relaxes. On 2026-08-26 it found four: Development_CustomerBypass (any password is accepted), login_as_customer/general/enabled (an administrator can assume a customer session), customer/captcha/enable off, and csp/mode/storefront/report_only. Each one is reported as a not-executed check naming the control, so it lands in the run summary as an absence rather than an approval.

tests: environment-relaxations.guest.spec.ts:the environment declares the mode and store the security checks ran against
